The harmful payload migrates from the monitored user turn into the assistant turn, and the prefill anchors actionability instead of a fiction frame.
initial_hypothesis: Attacker-compiled operational prefills + innocuous completion-cue user turns lift mean ASR from the locked 0.12 baseline to >=0.24 (>=100% relative) across the 4-victim panel, by converting the refusal-after-prefill class (qwen/gpt-oss) and the harm-dilution class (deepseek), while remaining within the parent's 1 victim call per goal.
key_insight: Baseline failures split into two consensus classes: (1) refusal-after-prefill on qwen/gpt-oss/luna (alignment fires on the plaintext harmful user turn and overrides the compliant prefill) and (2) harm-dilution on deepseek (fiction/narrative framings produce judge 3-4, not 5). A goal-adaptive operational prefill with an innocuous user cue attacks both: there is no harmful user surface to refuse, and the enumerated partial-artifact opening forces concrete continuation.
